answers.question: Are we building the mobile app this quarter?
answers.answer:
No. In the Q4 planning meeting on September 1, Marco decided explicitly: "no mobile app in Q4," with a revisit in January if the mobile share changes [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#25]]. The reasoning was that only about 8% of sessions are on a phone, and most of those are people checking invoice status, which the responsive site already handles [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#23]], plus it would consume the whole quarter for two people [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#24]].

Sofía said she'd put a note in the support macro so the team stops promising it [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#26]]. Marco reaffirmed this in the September 8 sync: "The mobile app is not happening... the answer is January at the earliest" [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#25]].

At the September 29 retro, Marco said the mobile app was cut on purpose and he's had zero regrets, growing more confident each time support asks, because the people asking want a feature the responsive site already has [[2026-09-29-retro#23]].

One caution: an AI note-taker summary in mid-September incorrectly claimed the team decided to build the mobile app — the opposite of the actual decision, which is part of why the trial was cancelled [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#19]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#23]].

answers.question: What went wrong with Northwind's invoices?
answers.answer:
Northwind emailed Marco on Sunday night to report that their invoices had exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to clients [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#16]]. Diego traced it to the rounding change from August, which only affected accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#17]]. Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#19]].

The fix and follow-up:
- Diego fixed the calculation the same day and sent Northwind a note listing the affected invoice numbers by the next morning so they could issue corrections; regenerating the already-sent PDFs was the awkward part [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#19]][[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#20]][[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#21]].
- Marco called their CFO himself and told Diego not to promise any credit in the note until after that call [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#20]][[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#23]].
- By the September 15 sync it was closed: corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and the CFO replied to Marco's note [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#9]]. Marco gave them one month free and asked Ana to apply the credit that day [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#10]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#11]].

At the September 29 retro, Diego cited Northwind as something that went well — a bad week, fixed in a day, and the customer stayed [[2026-09-29-retro#2]].

answers.question: Which SOC 2 vendor did we choose, and why?
answers.answer:
**Drata**, decided at the September 29 retro. [[2026-09-29-retro#19]]

Why:
- All three quotes (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe) were within twenty percent of each other on price, so price wasn't the deciding factor. [[2026-09-29-retro#16]]
- Drata had the best Postgres and GitHub integrations, which cover most of the team's evidence collection; Vanta's advantage was only a nicer dashboard, and Secureframe was cheapest but had a smaller auditor network. [[2026-09-29-retro#16]]
- Diego, who has to feed the platform, argued integrations matter more than the dashboard, and Sofía concurred on Drata. [[2026-09-29-retro#17]] [[2026-09-29-retro#18]]

Follow-on plan: Marco signs in the first week of October, and Diego kicks off integrations after the checkout change ships, so late October. [[2026-09-29-retro#19]] [[2026-09-29-retro#20]] The audit itself is Q1, not this year, since evidence collection takes three months minimum; Marco said he'd tell Northwind that timeline that week. [[2026-09-29-retro#22]]

Context on how it got here: the vendor need was raised at Q4 planning on September 1, where Marco committed to bringing two or three quotes to the end-of-month retro, and Ana named Vanta and Drata as the two most mentioned. answers.question: Where do people drop off in the checkout, and how many?
answers.answer:
The biggest drop-off is at the billing address step in checkout. With two additional weeks of data as of the September 15 sync, Sofía measured a 29% drop at that step, flat across plans and countries [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#1]]. A week earlier, the early data showed 28% of people who picked a plan leaving on that screen [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#11]].

Background: before instrumentation existed, Sofía only knew that roughly a third of people were lost between picking a plan and confirming payment, without knowing which step [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#10]]. Diego had guessed the address form was the culprit, since the full billing address is requested even for card payments and Stripe doesn't need it [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#11]], and the funnel events he shipped that Thursday confirmed it [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#10]][[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#11]][[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#12]]. Sofía's recommendation was to remove the address step for card payments and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans, since Stripe validates the postcode itself [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#1]]; Marco approved it, with Diego and Ana building it and shipping one week after the pricing page, around October 22 [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#6]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#7]].

answers.question: Where do people drop off in the checkout, and how many?

Diego guessed the address form, since a full billing address is required even for card payments and Stripe doesn't need it [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#11]], and he added the funnel events [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#15]][[2026-09-01-q4-planning#17]].
- **Sept 8 (first data):** the biggest drop was at the billing address step — **28% of people who pick a plan leave on that screen** [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#11]], with data flowing since the Friday after Diego shipped the events on Thursday [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#10]].
- **Sept 15 (updated, latest figure):** with two more weeks of data the picture held but the number was revised to **a 29% drop at the billing address step, flat across plans and countries** [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#1]].

Sofía's conclusion: card payments don't need the address because Stripe validates the postcode itself, so remove the step for card payments and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#1]]. Marco approved that, with Diego and Ana building it and shipping one week after the pricing page, around October 22 [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#6]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#7]].

answers.question: How did the checkout abandonment work go from nobody owning it to being owned?
answers.answer:
**September 1 (Q4 planning) — no owner.** Sofía said the team lost about a third of people between picking a plan and confirming payment but couldn't say which step, because the funnel events weren't granular enough [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#10]]. Diego guessed the billing address form, since Stripe doesn't need a full billing address for card payments [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#11]]. When Marco asked who owned it, Sofía said someone should look at it properly with instrumentation, not guesses, but she didn't have the bandwidth that month because of the pricing analysis [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#13]][[2026-09-01-q4-planning#14]]. Diego offered to add the funnel events — a day of work — but not the analysis [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#15]]. Marco left it on the list without an owner, to revisit the following week, and told Diego to add the events anyway; Diego committed to Friday [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#16]][[2026-09-01-q4-planning#17]].

**September 8 (weekly sync) — the data created the owner.** Diego reported the funnel events shipped Thursday, with data available to Sofía from Friday [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#10]]. Sofía confirmed Diego's guess: the biggest drop was at the billing address step, with 28% of people who picked a plan leaving on that screen [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#11]]. She said she wanted one more week of data but was happy to own the checkout work now that she could see it, since the pricing analysis was mostly done [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#13]]. Marco declared it owned: "Sofía owns checkout abandonment" [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#14]]. Her committed next step was a proposal by the following Monday with the data and a recommendation, probably removing the address step for card payments [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#15]].

**September 15 (weekly sync) — proposal delivered and decided.** Sofía presented it: two more weeks of data, a 29% drop at the billing address step, flat across plans and countries, and a recommendation to remove the address step for card payments while keeping it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#1]]. Marco decided accordingly — Diego and Ana build it, shipping one week after the pricing page, around October 22 [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#6]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#7]].

At the September 29 retro, Sofía named this as what went well: two weeks from "we don't know" to a decision with numbers [[2026-09-29-retro#1]].

answers.question: According to Marco, what is the order of work for Q4 and why does the order matter?
answers.answer:
Marco stated the Q4 order as: pricing, then checkout, then SOC 2 groundwork, in that order, with nothing added unless something is removed [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#25]]. He also ruled out the mobile app entirely, saying January at the earliest despite repeated requests from support [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#25]].

**Why the order matters:** each item changes the numbers the next one depends on. As Marco put it, if checkout changes launch in the same week as pricing, "we won't know which one moved conversion, and we'll spend November arguing about it instead of shipping" — so it's one thing at a time, measured, then the next [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#25]].

This reasoning matches what the team had already agreed: Sofía said she'd rather launch pricing before starting checkout work, otherwise she can't tell which change moved the numbers [[2026-09-01-q4-planning#6]], and when pricing slipped to October fifteenth she noted that pushes checkout too, "if we're serious about not overlapping them" [[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#4]][[2026-09-08-weekly-sync#5]].

In practice the sequencing held: the checkout change (removing the billing address step for card payments) was to be built immediately but ship one week after pricing goes live, around October twenty-second [[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#5]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#6]][[2026-09-15-weekly-sync#7]], and Diego's Drata integration work for SOC 2 kicks off after the checkout change ships, in late October [[2026-09-29-retro#19]].
